body.statement: Fix \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\). Under \(P\in\operatorname{ri}(C_c^v)\), the projected empirical law \(\widetilde P_n\) is eventually attainable almost surely and \(L_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\to L_c^v(P)\) and \(U_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\to U_c^v(P)\) almost surely.
body.justification: Convex endpoint values are relatively continuous at fixed-slope relative-interior attainable laws, and affine-hull projection preserves empirical convergence.
body.gap: The proof gives no attainable-boundary continuity and no joint consistency as \(c\) varies through one.
body.consumer: It justifies only pointwise fixed-slope plug-in endpoint estimation in the stated regime.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\) and \(v\in\{\mathrm w,+\}\), and abbreviate \(C=C_c^v\) and \(A=\operatorname{aff}(C)\).  The assumption \(P\in\operatorname{ri}(C)\) in particular implies that \(C\) is nonempty.

First, \(C\) is convex.  Take \(Q_0,Q_1\in C\), choose \(d_j\) in the fiber over \(Q_j\), and, using \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\), choose \(z_j\in\mathcal F_c^v(Q_j,d_j)\).  For \(0\le\lambda\le1\), all lift equalities are affine and every PSD block remains PSD under convex combination, because
\[
 a^{\mathsf T}\{\lambda M_0+(1-\lambda)M_1\}a
 =\lambda a^{\mathsf T}M_0a+(1-\lambda)a^{\mathsf T}M_1a\ge0.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \lambda z_0+(1-\lambda)z_1
 \in\mathcal F_c^v\bigl(\lambda Q_0+(1-\lambda)Q_1,
 \lambda d_0+(1-\lambda)d_1\bigr). \tag{1}
\]
The reverse implication of the all-laws theorem places the mixed law in \(C\), proving convexity for both the weak and strict classes.

The lower endpoint is convex on \(C\).  Indeed, for \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(d_j\) in the fiber over \(Q_j\) with
\[
 d_j<L_c^v(Q_j)+\varepsilon.
\]
Using (1) and then letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) gives
\[
 L_c^v(\lambda Q_0+(1-\lambda)Q_1)
 \le\lambda L_c^v(Q_0)+(1-\lambda)L_c^v(Q_1).
\]
Choosing \(d_j>U_c^v(Q_j)-\varepsilon\) instead proves that \(U_c^v\) is concave.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}slope\text{-}endpoints}\), both functions are finite on \(C\).  Extend \(L_c^v\) and \(-U_c^v\) by \(+\infty\) off \(C\).  They are proper convex functions with domain \(C\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}relative\text{-}interior\text{-}convex\text{-}continuity}\) at \(P\in\operatorname{ri}(C)\) shows that \(L_c^v\) and \(U_c^v\) are continuous at \(P\), relative to \(A\).

For completeness, the relative-interior premise forces positive observed cells even though the all-laws theorem does not require them.  Let \(\mu\) be unit mass at \(u=1\), set \(h_x(1)=1/2\), and set \(g_{xy}(z,1)=1/2\) for all \(x,y,z\in B\).  These kernels belong to both legal classes, and
\[
 P^\star(x,y,z,w)=\frac14p_x(y,1)p_z(w,1)>0
\]
for all sixteen cells, so \(P^\star\in C\).  If a coordinate \(P_j\) were zero, the relative-interior ball around \(P\) in \(A\) would contain \(P+\epsilon(P-P^\star)\) for sufficiently small \(\epsilon>0\); its \(j\)-th coordinate would equal \(-\epsilon P_j^\star<0\), contradicting \(C\subseteq\Delta^{15}\).  Thus \(P\) has positive cells.  This derived fact is not substituted for the relative-interior assumption.

It remains to control the empirical argument.  For one cell let \(Z_i\) be its indicator, put \(p=\mathbb E Z_i\), and set \(W_i=Z_i-p\).  Independence and centering imply that every term in the fourth-moment expansion vanishes unless every sample index occurs at least twice.  Since \(|W_i|\le1\),
\[
 \mathbb E\left[\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nW_i\right)^4\right]
 =\frac{n\mathbb E[W_1^4]+3n(n-1)\{\mathbb E[W_1^2]\}^2}{n^4}
 \le\frac{3}{n^2}. \tag{2}
\]
Hence, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \Pr\left(\left|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i\right|>\epsilon\right)
 \le\frac{3}{\epsilon^4n^2}. \tag{3}
\]
The probability of at least one such deviation after time \(N\) is at most \(3\epsilon^{-4}\sum_{n\ge N}n^{-2}\), which tends to zero.  Intersecting the resulting probability-one events over \(\epsilon=1/k\), \(k\in\mathbb N\), and over the sixteen cells proves
\[
 \widehat P_n\longrightarrow P\qquad\text{almost surely}. \tag{4}
\]

The affine space \(A\) is closed in the finite-dimensional cell space and contains \(P\).  The Pythagorean identity for orthogonal projection therefore gives
\[
 \|\widetilde P_n-P\|_2\le\|\widehat P_n-P\|_2. \tag{5}
\]
Equations (4)--(5) imply \(\widetilde P_n\to P\) almost surely.  Since \(P\in\operatorname{ri}(C)\), some relative open ball in \(A\) around \(P\) is contained in \(C\).  Therefore \(\widetilde P_n\in C\) eventually almost surely.  Relative continuity at \(P\) now yields
\[
 L_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\longrightarrow L_c^v(P),
 \qquad
 U_c^v(\widetilde P_n)\longrightarrow U_c^v(P)
\]
almost surely.  The proof holds at fixed \(c\) and uses the relative-interior ball essentially; it gives neither boundary continuity nor joint consistency as \(c\) varies through one.
